gaps: P0: none (#1, a Josua de Grave drawing, is undated and late 17th century). P5: only #28, left out for its date.
notes: The Le Loup drawing is dated 1738 by Commons but its inscription (as transcribed in the file name) says drawn in 1739, hence ‘1738–39’. P1 alternative: Blaeu’s colored bird’s-eye view (#4, 1649; the Rijksmuseum copies #10/#11/#13 of the same plate say 1652), more detailed but closer to a plan. P3 alternative: #15, the Prince-Bishops’ Palace (1838 steel engraving), sharper but a single building. #28 is a pre-war ‘Panorama général’ postcard stamped by a German unit in 1915; the photograph itself may be some years older, and the file is small (1024 px). P6 alternative: #32 (2022, sharp, but a construction crane in front) and #29 (2009 panorama, 3:1).
